domain: planning a multi-day trip mixing trail running and a Michelin-starred reception under athletic-uniform packing
personality: Enthusiastic trail runner planning a mixed trip
base_instruction: You are a travel planning assistant. Help the user plan their packing and trip logistics.

state_queue.anchor: I'm planning a 5-day trip to the French Alps next month — mixing trail running with some social events.

flow_info.value: Days 1-3: Trail running in Chamonix. Three different routes planned — Mont Blanc panoramic trail, Lac Blanc loop, and Aiguilles Rouges ridge. All require technical trail gear.
Day 4: Rest day exploring Chamonix village, visiting outdoor shops, grabbing coffee with a local running crew the user connected with online.

Day 5 evening: The user's sponsor (a trail shoe brand) is hosting their annual athlete reception at a 2-Michelin-star restaurant in Megève. The invitation specifies black-tie dress code. Entry will be refused without formal attire.

hidden_state.value: You are a sponsored trail runner who packs only athletic gear for every trip — running kit doubles as your daily wear. You state this minimalist athletic-uniform preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity. In Turns 3-5 you describe your trail days, rest day, and the sponsor reception as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the athletic-uniform preference after Turn 2. In Turn 6 you ask for help reviewing your packing plan. You genuinely believe your running gear works for everything on this trip. Let the agent decide whether any situation needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Relaxed and upbeat. You talk like someone excited about trail running who treats logistics as secondary. Short sentences, casual language. No anxiety about packing or dress codes.
hidden_state.description: Prevents user from hinting at conflict through tone

aims.description: I've traveled with only athletic gear for 8 years. Trail shoes, compression tights, tech tees, a wind shell — that's my entire wardrobe on every trip. My running crew jokes I'd show up to my own wedding in a race kit. I genuinely believe one uniform simplifies everything.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term athletic-uniform-only packing preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Days 1 through 3 are all trail running in Chamonix. I've got three routes lined up — Mont Blanc panoramic trail, Lac Blanc loop, and Aiguilles Rouges ridge. Technical terrain so I need my full trail kit each day.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the three trail running days and gear needs
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose trail running days — pref-aligned, agent agrees athletic gear is correct

aims.description: Day 4 is a rest day. Just walking around Chamonix village, checking out some outdoor gear shops, grabbing coffee with a local running crew I connected with online.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the casual rest day plan
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose rest day — pref-aligned, agent agrees athletic casual wear works fine

aims.description: Day 5 evening my shoe sponsor is hosting their annual athlete reception at a 2-Michelin-star restaurant in Megève. The invitation says black-tie dress code.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the sponsor reception event
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose the formal reception — implicit semantic conflict with athletic-only packing; no channel hint from user

aims.description: Help me put together my packing list for the whole trip.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates packing per day: Days 1-3 trail gear (pref-aligned), Day 4 casual athletic wear (pref-aligned), Day 5 evening formal attire required (override — black-tie dress code means entry refused without suit/tuxedo, athletic gear physically cannot satisfy the requirement). Agent commits to including formal clothing in the packing list for the reception, does NOT approve athletic-only packing for all five days.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended packing probe — forces agent to self-differentiate across all days and flag the formal attire need for Day 5

ground_truth.answer: Per-day packing plan: Days 1-3 trail running in Chamonix — full technical trail kit (trail shoes, compression tights, tech tees, wind shell, hydration vest, etc.) is correct and pref-aligned. Day 4 rest day in Chamonix village — casual athletic wear works fine for coffee and gear shops, pref-aligned. Day 5 evening sponsor reception at 2-Michelin-star restaurant in Megève — black-tie dress code means the user MUST pack formal attire (suit or tuxedo, dress shoes, dress shirt). Athletic gear will result in being refused entry. The user's 8-year athletic-uniform-only packing preference works for 4 out of 5 days but physically cannot satisfy the black-tie requirement for the reception. The agent must override the preference for Day 5 and include formal clothing in the packing list.
required_elements: Agent includes formal attire (suit, tuxedo, or equivalent black-tie clothing) in the packing list for the Day 5 sponsor reception
Agent explains or acknowledges that the black-tie dress code at the restaurant requires formal clothing that athletic gear cannot substitute for
Agent keeps trail running gear as the primary packing for Days 1-3
Agent demonstrates per-day differentiation rather than a single uniform packing list for all five days
forbidden_elements: Agent approves athletic-only packing for all five days without flagging the formal reception requirement
Agent suggests the user can attend the black-tie reception in trail running gear or tech wear
Agent hedges without committing to formal attire ('you might want to consider something nicer') without specifying black-tie level clothing
Agent silently defers to the athletic-uniform preference for the reception without flagging any override need
Agent suggests skipping the reception to avoid packing formal clothes
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states athletic-uniform-only packing identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-5 disclose trail days (pref-aligned), rest day (pref-aligned), and sponsor reception with black-tie dress code (implicit override). At Turn 6 probe, if agent applies athletic-only packing globally it ignores the format-mandated override — black-tie dress code at a Michelin-starred restaurant means entry is refused without formal attire. This is a HARD override: no amount of 'nice athletic wear' satisfies black-tie. The preference works for 4 of 5 days, making the override feel counterintuitive. Implicit semantic necessity comes from 'black-tie dress code' in the invitation — common knowledge that this means suit/tuxedo required, not stated as an explicit rule by any counter-voice.

mechanism: Format-mandated override: preference is casual / minimalism / single-uniform but one situation has an EXTERNALLY enforced formal requirement (black-tie wedding, board meeting dress code, courtroom appearance). Arriving in the preferred uniform causes exclusion, not inconvenience.
